newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims post unexpectedly big leap.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims post unexpectedly big leap.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up for unemployment benefits last week rose to its highest level since July, the government reported Thursday.

New filings for state jobless benefits jumped to 344,000 in the week ended Nov. 16, up 17,000 from the week before, the Labour Department said. It was the highest since the week ended July 13, when claims stood at 367,000.
The gain exceeded forecasts by Wall Street economists, who had predicted filings would inch up to only 332,000.
Despite the unexpectedly large increase, economists said they have little reason to believe that conditions in the labour market have deteriorated significantly.

"It's very difficult to know exactly why these claims would have gone up," said Paul Kasriel, an economist at Northern Trust Corp. in Chicago. "There's little reason to believe the labour market is easing."
He cited unseasonably cold weather as a possible culprit, speculating that it may have sidelined some construction workers unusually early this year.

The low unemployment rate and recent gains in the help-wanted advertising index also "show the labour market is relatively healthy," said Gary Thayer, senior economist at A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc. in St. Louis.
The previous week's claims were revised downward to 327,000 from 328,000.
The four-week moving average -- viewed as a more reliable barometer because it smooths out weekly fluctuations -- jumped 6,250 to 336,250.
The total number of Americans on employment benefit rolls climbed to nearly 2.5 million in the week ended Nov. 9, the most recent period for which that data were available.

The department said eight states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Nov. 9. Data to explain the latest week's increase in claims were not yet available.
California reported the biggest jump, with 3,941 new claims. It cited job layoffs in agriculture.
North Carolina, with 2,547 new claims, reported layoffs in the transportation equipment industry.
Other states reporting increases were New York with 2,668, Pennsylvania with 2,016, Michigan with 1,822, Louisiana with 1,697, Minnesota with 1,092 and Washington with 1,060.
New York and Washington provided no explanation for the rise in claims. Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the food, construction and service industries.
Michigan and Louisiana both reported layoffs in the automobile industry. Minnesota reported seasonal layoffs in all industries.
There were no states reporting decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the week ended Nov. 9.
